title: No MCP server implemented — the spec's central requirement is unmet
evidence: go.mod declares zero dependencies (no MCP SDK); grep for jsonrpc|stdio|tools/list|tools/call|initialize|protocol across all .go files finds nothing; cmd/main.go:24 blocks on `<-make(chan struct{})` after only printing match/player counts, with comments at main.go:22-23 conceding 'MCP server would be started here'. The Server/ExecuteQuery type in internal/server/server.go is never called from main.go or anywhere outside server.go (dead code) and is a plain in-process query dispatcher, not an MCP transport.
suggestion: Add an MCP server SDK dependency, wire an MCP stdio/JSON-RPC transport in main.go, and register the existing query handlers as MCP tools with input/output schemas.

title: Query dispatch layer (Server.ExecuteQuery) is never invoked
evidence: internal/server/server.go:40 ExecuteQuery and :19 NewServer are defined but grep shows no caller anywhere in the tree except within server.go; cmd/main.go never constructs a Server, so even the custom (non-MCP) query interface is unreachable at runtime.
suggestion: Wire NewServer(db).ExecuteQuery into the MCP tool handlers so the query engine is actually reachable.

title: All tests hardcode an ephemeral absolute data path
evidence: internal/store/store_test.go:9,26,40,50,64,79,94,112,129,162 pass '/Users/adriancockcroft/.retort/work/retort-local-0xabe5kx/retort-d5c30c1005b2/data/kaggle' to LoadData; this transient work dir will not exist on re-run, so the suite is non-portable and would fail outside the original run sandbox.
suggestion: Load from the repo-relative ./data/kaggle path (as cmd/main.go does) or a testdata fixture.
